title: Honours, Anthems & Holidays
subtitle: The Victoria Cross, O Canada, the Order of Canada, official languages and important dates

questions.question: What is the highest honour that Canadians can receive?
questions.explanation: The Victoria Cross (V.C.) is the highest honour available to Canadians. It is awarded for the most conspicuous bravery, a daring act of valour or self-sacrifice, or extreme devotion to duty in the presence of the enemy.

questions.question: How many Canadians have been awarded the Victoria Cross since 1854?
questions.explanation: The V.C. has been awarded to 96 Canadians since 1854.

questions.question: Who was the first Canadian to be awarded the Victoria Cross?
options: Alexander Roberts Dunn, in the Charge of the Light Brigade (1854)
questions.explanation: Lieutenant Alexander Roberts Dunn, born in present-day Toronto, served in the Charge of the Light Brigade at Balaclava (1854) in the Crimean War and was the first Canadian awarded the V.C.

questions.question: Who was the first black man to be awarded the Victoria Cross?
options: Able Seaman William Hall of Horton, Nova Scotia
questions.explanation: Able Seaman William Hall of Horton, Nova Scotia, whose parents were American slaves, was the first black man to be awarded the V.C., for his role in the Siege of Lucknow during the Indian Rebellion of 1857.

questions.question: Which First World War flying ace from Owen Sound, Ontario, earned the Victoria Cross?
questions.explanation: Flying ace Captain Billy Bishop, born in Owen Sound, Ontario, earned the V.C. in the Royal Flying Corps during the First World War and was later an honorary Air Marshal of the RCAF.

questions.question: Who was the last Canadian to receive the Victoria Cross to date?
options: Lieutenant Robert Hampton Gray, killed in August 1945
questions.explanation: Lieutenant Robert Hampton Gray, a navy pilot born in Trail, B.C., was killed while bombing and sinking a Japanese warship in August 1945, days before the end of the Second World War, and was the last Canadian to receive the V.C. to date.

questions.question: In what year was O Canada proclaimed as the national anthem?
questions.explanation: O Canada was proclaimed as the national anthem in 1980. It was first sung in Québec City in 1880. French and English Canadians sing different words.

questions.question: Where and when was O Canada first sung?
questions.explanation: O Canada was first sung in Québec City in 1880, a century before it was proclaimed the national anthem.

questions.question: What is the Royal Anthem of Canada?
questions.explanation: The Royal Anthem of Canada, "God Save the King (or Queen)," can be played or sung on any occasion when Canadians wish to honour the Sovereign.

questions.question: Complete the line from O Canada: "The true North ..."
questions.explanation: "With glowing hearts we see thee rise / The true North strong and free!" is from the English lyrics of O Canada.

questions.question: When did Canada start its own honours system with the Order of Canada?
questions.explanation: After using British honours for many years, Canada started its own honours system with the Order of Canada in 1967, the centennial of Confederation.
questions.ref: Discover Canada, The Order of Canada and Other Honours (p. 41)

questions.question: What are the three main objectives of the Official Languages Act of 1969?
options: Make every Canadian bilingual, abolish French schools, promote English abroad
Establish equality of French and English in Parliament and government; maintain official language minority communities; promote equality of French and English in society
Make French the language of Quebec only
Replace English with French in the civil service
questions.explanation: The Act's objectives: establish equality between French and English in Parliament, the Government of Canada and institutions subject to the Act; maintain and develop official language minority communities; and promote equality of French and English in Canadian society.

questions.question: On what date is Canada Day celebrated?
questions.explanation: Canada Day is July 1, marking the birth of the Dominion of Canada on July 1, 1867.

questions.question: When is Victoria Day?
options: The Monday preceding May 25, the Sovereign's birthday
questions.explanation: Victoria Day is the Monday preceding May 25 (the Sovereign's birthday).

questions.question: When is Thanksgiving Day in Canada?
questions.explanation: Thanksgiving Day is the second Monday of October. Labour Day is the first Monday of September.

questions.question: On what date is Sir John A. Macdonald Day?
questions.explanation: Sir John A. Macdonald Day is January 11, his birthday. Sir Wilfrid Laurier Day is November 20. Vimy Day is April 9. Boxing Day is December 26.

questions.question: What is celebrated in Quebec on June 24?
options: Fête nationale (Feast of St. John the Baptist)
questions.explanation: June 24 is the Fête nationale in Quebec, the Feast of St. John the Baptist.

questions.question: True or false: Remembrance Day is observed on November 11.
questions.explanation: True. Remembrance Day is November 11, marking the Armistice that ended the First World War in 1918.

questions.question: True or false: Queen Elizabeth II became Queen of Canada in 1952 and celebrated her Diamond Jubilee (60 years) in 2012.
questions.explanation: True. Queen Elizabeth II was Queen of Canada from 1952 until her death in 2022. She marked her Golden Jubilee in 2002 and Diamond Jubilee in 2012. Her son is now King Charles III.

questions.question: True or false: Ordinary citizens may nominate fellow citizens for honours such as the Order of Canada.
questions.explanation: True. If you know of fellow citizens who you think are worthy of recognition, you are welcome to nominate them.
questions.ref: Discover Canada, The Order of Canada and Other Honours (p. 41)
